title: GenAI critical-review lab and portfolio sorting task
summary: First-year web-programming students use Copilot to generate HTML and ChatGPT to review it, then critique and improve the output for semantics and accessibility. A later portfolio component requires an AI-generated sorting algorithm plus an explanation of the prompting and algorithmic reasoning.

sources.title: Stimulating Critical Thinking in a Web Programming Module with Generative AI Tools

locator.section: III. Implementation, B. Lab Sessions and Projects Assessment

sources.evidence_quote: We created an assessment for this module that instructed learners to utilise GitHub CoPilot and ChatGPT.

assessment.summary: Generate, review, critique, and improve web code with two AI tools, then apply AI prompting to a sorting component in a portfolio website.
student_actions: Use Copilot to generate an HTML table.
Evaluate the generated markup for semantic correctness and accessibility.
Use ChatGPT to review the Copilot output.
Critique ChatGPT's review and identify agreements and omissions.
Improve the code using semantic and accessibility principles.
Use GenAI to develop a portfolio-site sorting algorithm and explain the process and algorithm.

timing.release: Week 7 lab and later portfolio phase

student_role.description: Copilot acts as pair programmer and ChatGPT as peer reviewer; students must evaluate both outputs rather than accept them uncritically.

grading.method: Summative lab and portfolio assessment; no marks are awarded for a non-working algorithm or prompts too simple to reflect first-year taught content.
